name: Global food prices
summary: FAO food index at 136, up 5.8% on a year
state: The FAO Food Price Index rose 1.5% in September to 136.0, 5.8% above a year earlier and above the 135 Alert line (published 8 Oct). Cereals rose 5.1% and sugar 6.1%, driven by Black Sea logistics, dry weather and Hormuz shipping uncertainty. The October figure is due in the first week of November.
for_you: Food inflation is likely to stay elevated. Import-dependent poorer countries are most exposed.
rubric_hit: FFPI > 135, or multiple major exporters ban exports of a staple.

sources.title: MercoPress — FAO Food Price Index rises in September

why: Food prices drive inflation, hunger and political unrest; poorer countries spend up to half of income on food.
drivers: Harvests, weather, fertiliser and energy costs, export bans, conflict in breadbaskets.

rubric.alert: FFPI > 135, or multiple major exporters ban exports of a staple.
rubric.watch: FFPI 120–135, or y/y > +5%, or a major exporter restricts exports.
rubric.normal: FAO Food Price Index < 120 and y/y change < +5%.
